listRecheck.notes: Letter RTM confirmed on the Contra Costa and Santa Clara official lists. Alameda notice and San Mateo page show no letter. Ballot question identical across Alameda (two readings), Contra Costa and Santa Clara, apart from one comma noted.

measures.titleOnList: Contra Costa list: 'MEASURE RTM' / 'Regional Transit Measure'. Santa Clara list: 'Measure RTM' (Public Transit Revenue Measure District, 'Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative'). San Mateo page: 'Regional Transit Measure – Public Transit Revenue Measure District: Transactions and Use Tax Measure' (no letter shown). Alameda notice: no letter shown.
measures.titleNote: Our shortTitle 'Regional transit sales tax (Public Transit Revenue Measure)' is a description, not an official title. Official names seen are 'Regional Transit Measure' (Contra Costa, San Mateo) and 'Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative' (Santa Clara list). officialTitle could be set to 'Regional Transit Measure'.

ballotQuestion.text: To prevent major service cuts to BART and other transit, avoid increased traffic, and reduce pollution by: Preserving BART, Caltrain, VTA, SamTrans, AC Transit, Muni, other transit for everyone, including workers, students, seniors, persons with disabilities; Supporting transit safety, cleanliness, affordability, reliability; Repairing targeted roads/potholes; Requiring financial transparency, oversight, accountability; shall the measure enacting a 0.5% (Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, Santa Clara counties), and 1% (San Francisco) sales tax for 14 years generating approximately $980,000,000 annually, be adopted?
ballotQuestion.location: NOTICE OF GENERAL ELECTION, November 3, 2026 (Alameda ROV)
ballotQuestion.notes: Reader returned the question in segments; joined with single spaces. Read twice from the Alameda notice and once each from the Contra Costa list and Santa Clara list. All four readings agree word for word except that the Santa Clara reading shows no comma after 'Santa Clara counties)'. Alameda and Contra Costa both show the comma.

measureType.value: initiative; district transactions and use (sales) tax
measureType.evidence: San Mateo: 'Public Transit Revenue Measure District: Transactions and Use Tax Measure'. Alameda ROV memo quoting District Resolution No. 2: 'the Initiative Measure shall take effect in the District'.
measureType.notes: How the measure qualified as an initiative (petition or otherwise) was not stated in any document read.

threshold.notes: Read twice from the Alameda notice with the same result. Also stated by Contra Costa ('Majority Overall Required to pass'), Santa Clara ('Majority Vote Required') and San Mateo ('Majority Voter Approval Required'). Alameda ROV memo quoting District Resolution No. 2: 'if a simple majority of voters, assessed based on the cumulative vote within the entire district'. So the majority is counted across all five counties combined, not county by county.

fiscal.text: sales tax for 14 years generating approximately $980,000,000 annually, be adopted?
fiscal.notes: Alameda ROV memo (dated September 15, 2026, for the October 6, 2026 Board meeting) quotes the same figure and the recital 'for a duration of 14 years, and in an amount of 0.5% in the counties of Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, and Santa Clara'. The memo gives no start date and no Alameda County share; it says 'No net county cost will result from these recommended actions.'

fieldVerdicts.value: Adds a 0.5% sales tax in Alameda County (0.5% in Contra Costa, San Mateo and Santa Clara, 1% in San Francisco) for 14 years. The money goes to Bay Area transit operations and related road and rider improvements. [official notice; BOS memo]

fieldVerdicts.reason: Rates and 14 years are stated. 'Transit operations' and 'rider improvements' are not words in the ballot question; the official text lists preserving named transit systems, supporting transit safety, cleanliness, affordability, reliability, and repairing targeted roads/potholes. 'Operations' appears only in independent KQED text.
fieldVerdicts.proposedCorrection: Adds a 0.5% sales tax in Alameda County for 14 years. The rate is also 0.5% in Contra Costa, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties and 1% in San Francisco. [official notice]
